notes: Apply every case from a clean state: load dcasimulator/portfolio/index.html, dismiss any tour overlay, click #resetBtn, remove every portfolio left in #portfolioTabs with #delPortfolioBtn until only the portfolios listed in 'portfolios' remain, and click #clearPoolBtn (in #poolChipsWrap) if any asset is already loaded.
'settings' keys are DOM ids on the Settings tab (#randomSeed, #currencySymbol). Set #randomSeed BEFORE creating any simulated asset: the seed is what makes the synthetic price path reproducible.

'data' describes the Data tab. mode 'simulated': click the 'Simulated' button in #dataModeToggle, then for each entry of 'assets' fill #simNameInput / #simReturnInput / #simStdInput and click #addSimBtn. mode 'real': click 'Real', type the tickers into #tickerPoolInput and click #loadTickersBtn. Then set #startDate and #endDate.

'portfolios' is a list; create each with #addPortfolioBtn, rename it by double-clicking its tab, and fill it in the three sub-tabs of #pfEditSection. Assets sub-tab (#sub-assets): choose each asset in #assetPoolSelect and click #addAssetBtn. Top-Ups sub-tab (#sub-topups): #topupAmount, #topupYearlyInc, #topupPeriod, the schedule controls inside #topupScheduleBox, and the Risk-Free Account radios #rfOptRate / #rfOptTicker with #rfRate or #rfTicker. Rebalancing sub-tab (#sub-rebal): the method radios in #methodList (values towards-weight, constant-weight, constant-allocation, dynamic-momentum, rule-trigger; use #changeMethodBtn to reopen the list when it has collapsed), the per-asset target weights in #weightTableWrap, the momentum controls #lookbackMonths and #rankWeightTableWrap, the rule-based controls #reserveSelect and #triggerTableWrap, the Constant Weight timing radios (cwTiming values at-topup / schedule) with #rebalPeriod and #rebalScheduleBox, and the fees #buyFee and #sellFee.

Text/number inputs: set .value and dispatch 'input', 'change', 'blur'. Selects: set .value and dispatch 'change'. Radios: click the label. #topupAmount, #topupYearlyInc, #rfRate, #buyFee and #sellFee are formatted money inputs; give them a plain number string.

'schedule' keys and what they mean: day_of_month (the day a monthly schedule fires), quarter_month (which month of the quarter a quarterly schedule fires in, 1, 2 or 3), month_and_day (for a yearly schedule), anchor_date (the date a fortnightly schedule counts from), weekday.

'triggers' is a per-asset map filled in #triggerTableWrap. Trigger kinds, named as the Deploy Triggers tooltip names them: 'period-open' = a percentage move from the price at the start of each month or week; 'previous-top' and 'previous-bottom' = a percentage move against the highest / lowest close in the lookback window of bars before that day; 'technical' = the indicator rules the single-asset tool offers; 'at-topup' = invest at every top-up with no waiting. threshold_pct is the percentage move; lookback_bars is the rolling window length.

Run with #simBtn and wait until #summaryGrid has been rebuilt. Turn on #showAdvancedToggle when Sharpe / Sortino / CAGR are observed. Read: the per-portfolio tiles in #summaryGrid, the Breakdown Table in #compBody after choosing the portfolio in #detailPfSelect, the Composition chart series, #valueLegend / #priceLegend / #compLegend, #mainWarning, #dateRangeStatus / #poolStatus / #assetFetchStatus, #rateInfo, and the full daily CSV produced by #downloadBtn (use it wherever a per-bar or per-event series is needed).

Report numbers as plain numbers: strip currency symbols and thousands separators, keep the sign, and report a percentage as the number shown (9.7 for '9.7%'). Report text verbatim. Report a quantity that is absent, blank or shown as a dash as null rather than guessing.

Keys whose 'what' begins with 'Runner-computed' are arithmetic the runner performs on other observed values, on the displayed price series or on the daily CSV. Compute them from the same values reported for this case; never from anything inside _qa/plan/.

'bar index' means the 0-based position of a date in the run's trimmed date axis (row 0 of the daily CSV / the first plotted price point). A 'deploy' is an event in which reserve money is moved into an asset; a 'top-up' is a scheduled contribution arriving into the portfolio.
Cases with 'states' are several independent states. Apply each from a clean state and prefix that state's observation keys with the state name, exactly as the 'observe' keys are spelled.
A setup carrying "requires": "network" needs the live market-data worker. If it is unreachable, record the case as not-run (an error) rather than substituting anything.
Timezone states: relaunch the browser (or open a new Playwright context) with the named IANA zone - TZ env var or the context's timezoneId - and repeat the whole setup from scratch inside it.

nan_count means: the number of occurrences of 'NaN', 'Infinity', '-Infinity', 'undefined' or 'null' in the visible text of #summaryGrid, #compBody and #mainWarning (0 when there are none). js_error_count means the number of uncaught page errors and console errors captured while the case ran.

cases.title: Look-ahead: a trigger read from day D's close, and the reserve sale that funds it, cannot execute at day D's close

instructions: For every deploy into SIMA, recompute its own condition from the displayed close series: the condition is true on bar D when close(D) <= 0.95 * max(close(D-20) .. close(D-1)), i.e. five percent below the highest close of the twenty bars BEFORE D. The 'signal bar' of a deploy is the most recent bar at or before it at which that condition turned from false to true.

cases.title: Momentum ranking uses information available before the top-up bar

instructions: For each top-up bar D, compute each asset's trailing three-month return twice from the displayed closes: once ending at close(D) (the same-bar ordering) and once ending at close(D-1) (the causal ordering). Read the realised ordering from the share of that top-up deployed into each asset: 50% identifies rank 1, 30% rank 2, 20% rank 3.

observe.what: Number of top-up events.
Runner-computed: top-ups at which the same-bar ordering and the causal ordering are not the same ordering.
Runner-computed: among those, the number at which the realised ordering equals the same-bar ordering.
Runner-computed: among those, the number at which the realised ordering equals the causal ordering.
Runner-computed: topups_where_orders_differ - matched_prevBar_only.
Runner-computed: among those, the number at which the realised ordering equals neither.
Runner-computed: total deployed at top-ups / (1000 * n_topups).
See notes.
